methodology: Every insight below cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json or the underlying quarterly/*.json files; none are generic or asserted without a supporting number. Updated 2026-08-26 after a full Q1-Q3 quarterly backfill covering 2011-2025 (45 new quarterly files), which changed several conclusions from quarterly-only to the year-end (Q4/annual) view.

risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio surged from 30.0% (FY2023) to 67.1% (FY2024) to 56.5% (FY2025) and 55.7% (Q2 2026) — more than 10x the FY2011-2017 average of ~4.2%. The now-available quarterly granularity shows this was NOT a gradual build-up during 2024: NPL was still only 31.23% (Q1 2024), 30.75% (Q2 2024) and 31.01% (Q3 2024) — essentially flat — before jumping to 67.14% specifically within Q4 2024 (Oct-Dec) alone, a single-quarter recognition event rather than a multi-quarter drift.

Capital Adequacy Ratio fell from 10.26% (FY2023, above the ~10% regulatory minimum) to 3.47% (FY2024) and turned negative at -3.78% (FY2025) — the bank is capital-deficient against Basel III minimum requirements as of the latest reported figure.

ROE moved from +2.95% (FY2023) to -131.1% (FY2024) to -269.5% (FY2025). The quarterly backfill pinpoints the structural break earlier than the annual figures suggest: discrete net interest income was already negative in Q2 2024 (-693,932,503) and Q3 2024 (-792,875,189) — interest paid on deposits/borrowings exceeded interest income for two consecutive quarters before the FY2024 year-end NPL shock even hit — and cumulative 9-month 2024 net profit was still positive (+15,839,598) right up to Q3, meaning Q4 2024 alone produced a loss larger than the entire year's prior earnings.

Total equity turned negative in Q2 2025 (-12,829,192,612) — not merely 'FY2024' as the annual-only view implied — and has deteriorated in every single quarter since with no floor yet visible: +2,200,808,359 (Q1 2025) to -12,829,192,612 (Q2 2025) to -26,357,718,003 (Q3 2025) to -32,283,000,000 (FY2025 year-end) to -40,251,386,638 (Q1 2026) to -48,585,901,546 (Q2 2026). Six consecutive quarters of decline.

Total deposits have stayed broadly stable through the credit-quality collapse (~BDT 333bn FY2025 vs ~BDT 355bn FY2023 vs ~BDT 298bn FY2021) — based on the data collected, the stress is concentrated in capital and provisioning rather than a deposit run, though deposit costs (interest paid on deposits/borrowings) have risen and are a contributor to the negative net interest income noted above.

This is not the bank's first NPL shock, and the earlier one shows the current episode is qualitatively different. FY2018's NPL jump to 33.07% (per this dataset's Q4 series) peaked at 32.47% in Q1 2019 and was worked down gradually and steadily across four quarters (32.47% Q1 2019 to 28.41% Q2 2019 to 24.59% Q3 2019 to 18.28% Q4 2019) while equity and CAR stayed positive throughout. The 2024-2025 episode has shown no such recovery pattern in the six quarters of data collected since — equity has fallen every single quarter instead.

historical_context: With the full 2011-2025 Q1-Q3 quarterly series now on file (15 years, 45 quarters), ABBANK's pre-crisis history shows two distinct weak patches, both survived: (1) 2017-2018, when a large Q1 2017 provision expense (1,740,321,934, versus ~200-500m in a typical quarter) drove profit before tax briefly negative and Q3 2017 repeated the pattern (net loss -218,510,442) — the opening act of the FY2018 NPL jump to 33.07%; and (2) that FY2018 shock's aftermath, worked down gradually across 2019 (see risk_signals) back to a stable footing by FY2020-2023 (NPL 14-20%, CAR ~10-11%, positive ROE each year). The FY2024-2025 deterioration is a much larger, structurally different event: net interest income itself went negative for sustained periods (not just elevated provisioning), and equity — which never went negative in either of the two earlier weak patches — has now been negative for six consecutive quarters with no sign of bottoming. This matches the documented sector-wide Bangladesh banking asset-quality crisis of 2024-2025 but ABBANK's own severity and equity impact go beyond the median bank in this dataset.
data_gaps: Q1-Q3 quarterly granularity is now available for all 15 years 2011-2025 (45 quarters), closing what was previously this bank's largest data gap. Two residual, genuine (not research) gaps remain: (1) the 2017 Q3 filing (financial-statment-September-2017.pdf) contains no loan-classification breakdown anywhere in the document — confirmed by exhaustive search — so classified_loans_*/unclassified_* fields are absent from 2017_Q3.json specifically, though all other fields for that quarter are complete; (2) provision-coverage ratio, ROA and ROE are not calculable for any Q1-Q3 quarter in this dataset (only Q4/annual) because the unaudited interim filings do not disclose the loan-loss-allowance balance sheet account or a usable CAR figure the way annual reports do — this is a structural feature of Bangladeshi banks' interim disclosure, not a one-off omission. A 2010 H1 filing was found and its text archived (annual_reports/ABBANK/abbank-2010-h1-unaudited.txt) but not converted to a quarterly/*.json file, since this dataset's own FY2010 Q4/annual anchor doesn't exist for ABBANK (its Q4 series starts FY2011) — a future session could add it as a standalone supplementary point if useful.
